title: Notes Repository
prompt: Implement init_notes(conn) creating notes(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, body TEXT NOT NULL) and class NotesRepository(conn) with add(title, body) -> int (translate UNIQUE violation to ValueError 'duplicate title'), search(term) -> list[dict] of notes whose title CONTAINS term (LIKE with parameter-bound pattern; survives the injection test), and delete(note_id) -> bool.

tests.name: add, duplicate translated
tests.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
init_notes(conn)
repo = NotesRepository(conn)
nid = repo.add('meeting', 'agenda')
try:
    repo.add('meeting', 'again')
    failed = False
except ValueError as e:
    failed = 'duplicate title' in str(e)
assert failed
tests.hint: UNIQUE in schema; IntegrityError → ValueError('duplicate title').

tests.name: search matches substrings
tests.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
init_notes(conn)
repo = NotesRepository(conn)
repo.add('team meeting', 'x')
repo.add('meetup', 'y')
found = repo.search('meet')
assert {n['title'] for n in found} == {'team meeting', 'meetup'}
tests.hint: LIKE '%' || ? || '%' — the pattern is bound, not formatted.

tests.name: injection via search is inert
tests.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
init_notes(conn)
repo = NotesRepository(conn)
repo.add('safe', 'b')
assert repo.search("%' OR '1'='1") == []
tests.hint: Parameter-bound LIKE treats the payload as a literal substring.

tests.name: delete reports reality
tests.code:
import sqlite3
conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
init_notes(conn)
repo = NotesRepository(conn)
nid = repo.add('gone', 'x')
assert repo.delete(nid) is True
assert repo.delete(nid) is False
tests.hint: DELETE ... WHERE id = ?; rowcount decides True/False.
